import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sum of two squares, a power of 3, and a power of 5

Any integer $n > 1$ can be written as $a^2 + b^2 + 3^c + 5^d$ where $a, b, c, d$ are
nonnegative integers.

Zhi-Wei Sun has offered a \$3,500 prize for the first proof.

*References:*
- [A303656](https://oeis.org/A303656)
- Z.-W. Sun, "Restricted sums of four squares," arXiv preprint:
  https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05868v10
- Z.-W. Sun, "Refining Lagrange's four-square theorem," Journal of Number Theory:
  http://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/RefineFourSquareTh.pdf
- Z.-W. Sun, "Restricted sums of three or four squares":
  http://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/Square-sum.pdf
- Zhi-Wei Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture and variations:
  https://www.aimspress.com/aimspress-data/era/2020/2/PDF/1935-9179_2020_2_589.pdf
-/

namespace OeisA303656

/-- The predicate that `n` can be written as $a^2 + b^2 + 3^c + 5^d$ for nonnegative integers. -/
def A (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c d : ℕ, n = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + 3 ^ c + 5 ^ d

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : A 2 :=
  ⟨0, 0, 0, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : A 3 :=
  ⟨1, 0, 0, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : A 4 :=
  ⟨1, 1, 0, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : A 5 :=
  ⟨0, 1, 1, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_6 : A 6 :=
  ⟨0, 0, 0, 1, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_25 : A 25 :=
  ⟨1, 4, 1, 1, by norm_num⟩

/--
**Zhi-Wei Sun's Conjecture (A303656)**: Any integer $n > 1$ can be written as the sum of two
squares, a power of 3, and a power of 5.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : A n := by
  sorry

end OeisA303656

findings.description: The final reference is labelled “Zhi-Wei Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture and variations,” but its AIMS Press URL points to an unrelated paper about quadratic residues. This is a bibliographic error; the Lean conjecture is faithfully supported by the OEIS entry and arXiv:1701.05868v10.
findings.source_evidence: The first page of https://www.aimspress.com/aimspress-data/era/2020/2/PDF/1935-9179_2020_2_589.pdf identifies it as Fedor Petrov and Zhi-Wei Sun, “Proof of some conjectures involving quadratic residues,” Electronic Research Archive 28(2) (2020), 589–597, DOI 10.3934/era.2020031. Its abstract concerns quadratic residues modulo odd primes, not the 1-3-5 conjecture or A303656.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove this unrelated reference or replace its URL with the intended reference. The exact source for the formalized conjecture is already present: arXiv:1701.05868v10, Conjecture 4.1(i) and Remark 4.1.

findings.description: The reference described as the Journal of Number Theory article “Refining Lagrange's four-square theorem” links instead to Sun's presentation of the same title. The publication attribution and linked document do not match.
findings.source_evidence: http://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/RefineFourSquareTh.pdf opens with “A talk given at Zhejiang Univ. … and Nankai Univ.” and is a 50-slide presentation dated December 2, 2016. The actual article's source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/1604.06723 identifies the publication as J. Number Theory 175 (2017), 167–190; OEIS A303656 supplies its DOI, 10.1016/j.jnt.2016.11.008.
findings.suggested_fix: Link the journal citation to https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnt.2016.11.008 or https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.06723. Alternatively, retain the existing PDF and label it as the 2016 talk/slides.

reformulations.difference: OEIS defines a numerical count of representations with a ≤ b, whereas A is an existence predicate without that ordering restriction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A representation can be normalized by swapping a and b without changing the sum. Conversely, every normalized representation satisfies A. The representation set is finite: each variable is at most n, using a ≤ a², b ≤ b², c < 3^c, and d < 5^d. Thus A n is equivalent to positivity of the normalized representation count. The scratch file proves ordered_iff and positive_count_iff, and also proves equivalence of the universally quantified conjectures.

reformulations.difference: Sun's paper also expresses Conjecture 4.1(i) as the set equality {a²+b²+3^c+5^d : a,b,c,d ∈ N} = {2,3,4,…}; Lean states representability for every n > 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every represented number is at least 2, since each power is at least 1 and the squares are nonnegative. The reverse inclusion in the paper's set equality is therefore automatic; representability of every n > 1 supplies the other inclusion. This equivalence is proved as set_equality_iff in the scratch file.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in any of the eight declarations. The only findings are minor reference errors. The OEIS source still records the claim as a conjecture and reports verification through 2.4×10^11, consistent with research open. Direct OEIS access was blocked, so its official data mirror was used. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors or warnings: it proves nonrepresentability of 0 and 1, independently checks all six test witnesses, and proves the stated equivalences without sorry. Computed normalized counts match all 90 published OEIS terms, and a search finds representations for every 2 ≤ n ≤ 1000. No repository files were changed.
